passage: Welcome to our Science FAQ on Electric Circuits! Many students ask how we represent components. In a circuit diagram, a battery consists of two or more cells connected together, whereas a single cell is represented by a longer, thinner line for the positive terminal and a shorter, thicker line for the negative terminal. When a circuit is open, there is a gap, meaning the current cannot flow at all, rather than just stopping at the switch. Regarding safety, an electric fuse is a device that protects circuits by melting and breaking the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, rather than slowing down the flow. Furthermore, when current flows through a wire, it creates a magnetic field around it, even if the wire is not touching the compass needle. Finally, remember that an electromagnet is a temporary magnet that only acts as a magnet when current flows through its coil. Increasing the number of turns in the coil actually makes the electromagnet stronger, not weaker, because it increases the magnetic effect produced by the current. Understanding these basics helps us use electricity safely and effectively in our daily lives.

items.evidence: When a circuit is open, there is a gap, meaning the current cannot flow at all, rather than just stopping at the switch.
items.q: A switch is turned off, leaving a gap in a circuit. What happens to the current?
options: No current flows anywhere in the circuit
It flows up to the switch, then halts
It flows through the gap more slowly
It flows only in the part near the cell
items.explain: A gap in an open circuit stops the current everywhere; it does not travel part-way and stop.

wrong.why: thinks current reaches the switch and stops there
thinks a gap only slows the current
thinks current is used up before the gap

items.evidence: Regarding safety, an electric fuse is a device that protects circuits by melting and breaking the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, rather than slowing down the flow.
items.q: How does a fuse protect a circuit when the current becomes too high?
options: Its wire melts and opens the circuit
Its wire reduces the current gradually
Its wire grows thicker and carries more
Its wire stores the extra current safely
items.explain: A fuse melts when current is too high, which breaks the circuit; it does not slow the flow.

wrong.why: thinks a fuse slows down the current
thinks a thicker fuse wire is safer
thinks the fuse uses up the current

items.evidence: Furthermore, when current flows through a wire, it creates a magnetic field around it, even if the wire is not touching the compass needle.
items.q: A compass needle turns when placed near a live wire without touching it. Why?
options: The current makes a magnetic field around the wire
The wire becomes a permanent magnet itself
The needle is pulled by static electricity
The compass needs to touch the wire to turn
items.explain: Current creates a magnetic field around the wire, so the needle turns without touching it.

wrong.why: thinks electricity makes a permanent magnet
mixes up electricity and magnetism as the same
thinks the wire must touch the compass

items.evidence: Increasing the number of turns in the coil actually makes the electromagnet stronger, not weaker, because it increases the magnetic effect produced by the current.
items.q: Meena winds more turns of wire in her electromagnet's coil. What happens to its strength?
options: It becomes stronger as the effect adds up
It becomes weaker as the wire is longer
It stays the same since current is fixed
It stays on even after the current stops
items.explain: More turns increase the magnetic effect of the current, so the electromagnet becomes stronger.

wrong.why: thinks longer wire means weaker magnet
thinks coil turns do not affect strength
thinks an electromagnet is a permanent magnet
